name: Enoxaparin
summary: A low-molecular-weight heparin with predictable subcutaneous absorption and fixed weight-based dosing, used for VTE prophylaxis and treatment.
mechanism: Binds and potentiates antithrombin III, whose complex then inhibits factor Xa and, to a lesser extent, thrombin; higher anti-Xa to anti-IIa ratio than unfractionated heparin.
pharmacodynamics: Predictable anti-Xa activity; less protein and cell binding than unfractionated heparin, giving more consistent effect.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic depolymerization and renal clearance; no CYP involvement

dosing.adult: VTE prophylaxis: 40 mg SC once daily; VTE treatment: 1 mg/kg SC every 12 h (or 1.5 mg/kg once daily)
dosing.renalAdjustment: Reduce dose if CrCl <30 mL/min (e.g., 1 mg/kg once daily for treatment); consider anti-Xa monitoring

safety.pregnancy: May be used when anticoagulation is required (does not cross the placenta)
contraindications: Severe hypersensitivity to heparin or pork products
warnings: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (less common than with UFH)
Protamine sulfate only partially reverses LMWH
monitoring: Anti-Xa activity in renal impairment, extremes of weight, or pregnancy

indications: VTE prophylaxis (surgery, acute medical illness, immobility)
clinicalPearls: Predictable SC absorption allows fixed weight-based dosing without routine monitoring.
Preferred over unfractionated heparin in pregnancy because it does not cross the placenta.
bad: Patients with severe renal impairment or prior HIT; neuraxial anesthesia timing must be respected.
